the_cut: THE THREAD TRAVELS; THE PROCESS STAYS. A path is TRAVELS if a seat resuming on the other machine is a DIFFERENT seat without it. It is STAYS if it describes this machine's disk, ports, pids, byte offsets, microphone or raw ore. It is REGENERATES only if a NAMED writer rewrites it at a NAMED time, unasked. Anything else is UNDECIDED and says what would decide it.
limits: A CLASSIFICATION IS NOT A TRANSPORT. Every TRAVELS entry except letters.json, panes.json and resonance/topics is APPEND-ONLY JSONL. Two machines appending between syncs conflict at the tail of every one of them. TRAVELS is therefore conditional on the single-live-host guard (P-LIVE-HOST, E) plus pull-before-launch. Without both, this manifest names a merge-conflict set.
board.jsonl ALONE exceeds GitHub's 100 MB hard limit as measured. The transport question is decided by the compacted number, not by this file.

The classification is relative to THIS transport (a state repo; transcripts machine-local). dev/migrate/pack_room.ps1 classifies the same paths for a DIFFERENT transport (a private bundle in which transcripts DO travel) and disagrees on tailer-offsets.json and transcript-asks.jsonl. Both are right for their own transport; neither generalises. Do not merge the two sets.
REGENERATES states the consequence of arriving absent, because 'it comes back' and 'it comes back CORRECT' are not the same claim.

THE ROSTER AND THE SWEEP ARE ONE MECHANISM AND ARE WRITTEN IN TWO FILES. panes.json is read by read_kept() (main.rs:3320), and gc_captures() (main.rs:869) builds its keep-set from exactly that call — so WHICHEVER ROSTER THIS MANIFEST CAUSES TO BE ON DISK AT LAUNCH DECIDES WHICH CAPTURE TAILS SURVIVE, and the tails are the thread. The two are correct separately and neither says so. Measured 2026-09-09: the arrived and local id sets were DISJOINT, so classing this file STAYS would have swept all four arrived tails and the laptop's work would never have reached the desktop; adopting it swept D's five instead, which is the ruled retirement (revivable, in captures/archive) and not the same event. C added LIBRARIAN_SID to the keep-set at 7e6223e the same morning, one level down in the same function. Change either side and read the other.

out_of_root.decided_by: THE FOURTH STATE, USED (packet_state_set_2026-09-09.md section 5: a path that cannot be honestly placed says so, and says what would decide it). These directories are not under this manifest's root (data_dir), so no rule here can walk, classify or carry them — and panes.json is the only TRAVELS file that points outside its own transported tree (B, desktop_first_launch_2026-09-09.md section 0.7). They are not TRAVELS: a sibling dir holds a CLAUDE.md that warm_resume_brief rewrites from the seat's own travelled capture tail (main.rs:5379), so shipping the dir would carry a stale intake over a fresh one. They are not STAYS either, because a STAYS path is one the other machine does not need, and this one must EXIST at the destination or the seat it names cannot spawn. WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT: a second manifest rooted at instances_dir, or a rule form that can classify a path by reference from another root. Until then the transform mints what is missing and the reconciliation checks it landed — a mechanism, not a promise. This entry exists so that the next path pointing out of root cannot be added without saying the same.

THE KEPT ROSTER, AND IT DOES NOT DESCRIBE THE LIVE PANES — IT CREATES THEM. ui/term.js:1051 calls restoreKeptPanes() at module top level, which reads this file through list_kept_panes and SPAWNS one pane per row with its cwd verbatim. It travels because the keeper ruled it (one_house_two_machines_idea_2026-09-08.md:48: the laptop's seats become THE seats on both machines, committee panes named explicitly), so the pane IDS and LABELS are adopted — the ids key the capture tails, which are the thread. THE cwds ARE NEVER ADOPTED. This entry previously carried a precondition claiming the file travels correctly if both machines resolve the same instances_dir; that check PASSES here (both resolve C:\Consonance\instances) AND THE FAILURE HAPPENED ANYWAY, because what is machine-bound is not the root, it is the sibling-<id> directories minted inside it — 0 of 4 arrived cwds resolved on D while all 5 of its own did. A precondition is prose and cannot fail; the condition is now the on_arrival transform, which runs at the install boundary and is reconciled against the destination afterwards.

THE THIRD PLACE'S RECORD, AND IT IS FIRST IN THIS FILE BECAUSE FIRST MATCH WINS. The keeper's standing rule (.gitignore, 2026-08-29): the Third Place's record never goes to the repo and never to a cloud he did not choose. It migrates by hand or not at all. Found by C (P-SYNC-AT-LAUNCH section 6a) and carried by the chair as an interrupt. THE FAILURE WAS A WILDCARD NOBODY WROTE AGAINST IT: `captures/*.txt` below was written about the warm-resume carriers and silently swallowed a seat the rule forbids. A rule can be right about every case its author had in mind and still be wrong, because a glob has no idea what it is for.

the same seat's RETIRED tail, 80 KB, and it is the half the interrupt did not name. It reached the remote because of MY OWN change one rule below — captures/archive/*.txt UNDECIDED -> TRAVELS, made this packet on a correct ruling about revivability that says nothing about WHOSE record. Retired does not lift the keeper's rule; if anything a retired Third Place tail is more of its record, not less.

rules.why: P-LIVE-HOST's record and offline fallback (design §8). SHARED STATE ABOUT MACHINES: its entire purpose is that the other machine reads it and learns who holds the house — a copy that never leaves is a guard talking to itself. Note the asymmetry with install_id below, which is the opposite requirement and not a mirror of this one: live_host.json must be IDENTICAL on both machines; install_id must be UNIQUE to each. Same subject, opposite invariants.
rules.limit: TRAVELS does not make a heartbeat live. This file moves at sync cadence, so its freshness is bounded by the last pull and it cannot see a host that started since. E's design already puts the authority in the git lease for exactly this reason (design §4, §8) — the classification carries the record, not the liveness.

rules.why: RESERVED, does not exist. E's design needs a `syncVerified` input and §9 asks A for 'a sync-completion record the launcher can read'; absenceClass() treats null as UNKNOWN and refuses to read an absent claim without it. It answers 'did THIS machine's pull complete and verify' — per-machine, per-sync. If it travelled, machine D would read machine L's verification as its own, which is install_id's silent failure in a second costume: foreign state read as self.
rules.reservation: THE NAME IS MINE, THE FILE IS E's AND C's. If they choose a different name this rule must be renamed with it. Until then the checker catches the real name as UNPLACED, which is the correct outcome and better than a rule that pretends to cover a name nobody has picked.

rules.why: DECLARED IN ADVANCE, does not exist. C's replay-check.js writes it (`CONSONANCE_REPLAY_MARK`, :36) as a mark on this machine's board AND its transcripts, and splits later board growth into live turns versus replay by comparing the two. The transcripts are machine-local, so a mark taken on L and read on D would attribute D's board growth against transcripts D does not have. C's tool already refuses to score across a compaction on the grounds that the two are not the same corpus and a verdict across that seam is arithmetic on sand — a foreign mark is that same seam, one machine over. Found by running js-suite rather than by being told about it.
rules.reservation: the path is C's, from replay-check.js:36. If C renames it this rule must follow, and until then the checker catches the new name as UNPLACED.

rules.why: DECLARED IN ADVANCE; does not exist yet. P-BOARD-COMPACT (B) will move the pre-compaction board here as its reversibility. It must not travel: it is exactly the bytes the compaction removed, and carrying them would undo the only thing that gets the transport under the cap.

DECLARED IN ADVANCE, does not exist yet. C's launcher writes it (P-SYNC-AT-LAUNCH section 6e): which seats THIS machine adopted from the pulled state and which of its own it retired. Per-machine by construction — a travelled copy would tell the laptop it had adopted the desktop's retirements, which is sync-completion.json's failure in a fourth costume. Named explicitly rather than by a `sync-*` glob, and that is the lesson of this very packet: a wildcard is what put the Third Place's tail on GitHub. A future sync-* file this rule does not name shows as UNPLACED, which is the loud outcome and the correct one.
same packet, same seat: the launcher's own trace of what THIS machine pulled and when. A local log of a local operation.

DECLARED WITH THE CODE THAT WRITES IT (state-sync.js --push, L054). The RECEIPT of this machine last push: which outcome, which checks ran, and the run id of the process that wrote it, so close.js can gate on WHAT HAPPENED instead of on an exit code that four outcomes share. Per-machine by construction and STAYS for the same reason as state-sync.status.json and sync-completion.json: a travelled copy would tell the desktop that the laptop push was its own, which is install_id silent failure in a fifth costume. Named in full rather than by a state-sync.* glob -- the wildcard is what put the Third Place tail on GitHub, and a future file this rule does not name shows as UNPLACED, which is the loud outcome and the correct one.

DECLARED IN ADVANCE by the tool that writes it (state-sync.js, L052). It holds ONE COMMIT HASH PER MACHINE as of THIS machine last syncing, and chain-status.js reads it every prompt in place of the old "this machine only". It is a per-machine AS-OF view: if it travelled, the desktop would print the laptop's reading of both heads as its own and the in-sync line would report agreement it never checked. Same failure as install_id and sync-completion.json, third costume.

DECLARED IN ADVANCE; does not exist yet. state-sync.js --install moves any file it is about to overwrite here before writing the pulled one, so a sync that arrives wrong is reversible on the machine it arrived at. It is exactly the bytes the sync displaced -- carrying them back is how a bad sync becomes permanent on both machines.

forbidden.why: install_id MUST NOT LIVE UNDER THIS ROOT AT ALL — and this is a refusal of the placement asked for, not a naming of it. STAYS was the requested column and STAYS would not have worked: live-host.js's identityHazard() tests whether the install-id path sits inside the travelling root BY PATH PREFIX (:252-262). It never reads this manifest. So a STAYS rule here would keep the file out of the sync and STILL trip the hazard, and E's launcher would refuse to arm the guard — while the manifest read as having satisfied the dependency. A rule that looks like compliance and blocks the thing it was asked for is worse than no rule. Its home is machine-local and OUTSIDE the data dir: ~/.consonance.json already carries machine_tag, is already the machine-local identity file this room reads (actors.js, the MACHINE-BOUND class), and is already outside every travelling set. THE STAKE, in E's words: if that file ever lands in the travelling set both machines share an identity and every foreign claim reads as self — the guard returns PROCEED_RECLAIM at exactly the moment it should refuse, quietly, with no error anywhere. This declaration is what makes that loud.
same, one level down — a subdirectory of the data dir is still inside the travelling root, and the prefix test does not care how deep it is.
